question: Stars born in the Milky Way's first billion years that still shine are nearly all less massive than the Sun. Why?
options: Bigger ones burned out long ago
The first stars were all small
Old stars shed most of their mass
answer: Bigger ones burned out long ago. Blue stars ten times the Sun's mass last a few tens of millions of years; only the small, slow-burning ones outlive 12 billion. The survivors carry the dead giants' ashes: the heavy elements in one ancient star, SMSS J0313-6708, came from a single supernova of a massive first-generation star.
move: Judge a generation by who was born, not by who is left.
trap: Reading today's survivors as a fair sample of what was born.
reference: Keller et al., A single low-energy, iron-poor supernova as the source of metals in the star SMSS J031300.36-670839.3, Nature 506, 463, 2014
